workData.title:
Pocket Change
Poke Pay
workData.subTitle: Delivered seamless currency exchange experiences through branding, web, and kiosk UX/UI, driving a 140% sales increase.

content.text: “Pocket Change” is an innovative technology company revolutionizing foreign currency exchange with kiosks installed across Japan. These kiosks allow users to exchange foreign currency, recharge transportation IC cards, and convert leftover balances into points or e-money for other services.

As the Lead Product Designer, I developed the company’s branding, corporate identity, design system, and website. I also designed intuitive, multilingual interfaces for the kiosks to ensure accessibility for a diverse, international user base.

Pocket Change aimed to simplify foreign currency exchange by providing a seamless solution for travelers, while expanding its range of services with e-money and voucher partnerships worldwide. By focusing on user accessibility and convenience, the company sought to position itself as the go-to currency exchange service in Japan.
: Accepts 10 different currencies, with plans for further expansion.
: Offers a wide variety of global options, including PayPal, WeChat, Rakuten, and Amazon Gift Certificates, along with public transportation e-money like Rakuten Edy, WAON, and nanaco.
: Allows users to donate leftover currency to organizations like UNICEF.
: 80 kiosks installed nationwide, including major airports in Japan.
A visually appealing, intuitive kiosk interface and website will improve user engagement and satisfaction.
Expanding currency and e-money options will attract more users and increase transaction volume.
Promoting the service’s wide coverage and diverse offerings will enhance brand awareness and trust.
Established a cohesive brand image, creating high-quality photographs of kiosks, employees, and locations.
Designed a comprehensive design system to ensure consistency across digital and physical touchpoints.
Built a responsive corporate website from scratch, aligning it with the company’s mission and showcasing its features, coverage, and partnerships.
Developed an intuitive, multilingual kiosk interface to cater to international users, focusing on graphical designs to transcend language barriers.
Highlighted the seamless process for exchanging currency, recharging IC cards, and converting balances into vouchers or donations.
Incorporated messaging about expanding currency offerings and new partnerships to build user trust and confidence.
Enhanced the service’s usability by adding features like detailed instructions and an instructional video to the website.
: “Pocket Change” won the Good Design Award in 2018 for its innovative service and user-friendly design.
: 80+ kiosks installed nationwide, including major airports, serving millions of users annually.
: Partnered with international services like PayPal and WeChat, as well as Japan-specific e-money providers like Rakuten Edy and WAON.
: Multilingual and visually intuitive designs improved accessibility and satisfaction for international travelers.
: Designing for continuous service and currency expansion is essential for long-term growth.
: Multilingual support and partnerships with local services like Japanese e-money providers increase user trust and engagement.
: Combining digital platforms (website) and physical kiosks in a seamless ecosystem maximizes user adoption.

This project successfully positioned “Pocket Change” as a trusted, innovative solution for currency exchange, leveraging thoughtful design and strategic partnerships to serve both international travelers and domestic users, while addressing financial challenges for sustainable growth.

next.title: MYCITY
next.subTitle: Redesigned MYCITY’s website and app for clarity and usability while shaping MyPlace for Office, an IoT-powered smart office solution.

content.text: I joined MYCITY, a company specializing in behavior analysis technology through IoT devices, as a Product Designer to redesign their website and app. My goal was to enhance clarity and usability, ensuring their complex services were effectively communicated and user-friendly.

Additionally, I contributed to the design of “MyPlace for Office”, an IoT-powered smart office service that helps employees find optimal workspaces, track colleagues, and manage office resources efficiently.
The MYCITY website previously lacked depth and clarity, making it difficult to explain its advanced IoT solutions, including:
Illustrations would effectively communicate MYCITY’s services while avoiding visual clutter.
An intuitive interface would improve engagement and comprehension for website and app users.
Used illustrations to simplify complex IoT concepts and enhance visual appeal.
Developed a comprehensive design system for consistency across platforms.
Created a user-friendly interface for location tracking, air conditioning control, and congestion monitoring.
Focused on clear navigation and minimalistic layouts to streamline usability.
Expanded the website with instructional visuals to improve service understanding.
Integrated real-time data visualization for workplace tracking and optimization.
The redesigned website improved user understanding and client engagement by presenting MYCITY’s services clearly.
The MyPlace for Office app streamlined employee tracking, gaining positive feedback for its usability and workplace optimization features.
Simplified visuals, such as illustrations, are effective in explaining complex IoT services.
User-friendly designs paired with advanced IoT technology improve client trust and platform adoption.
Integrating user feedback into design strategies ensures seamless, scalable solutions.
This project positioned MYCITY as a leader in behavior analysis and IoT technology, delivering tools that enhance workplace productivity and user experience.
